traits.note: Britton and Rose's The Cactaceae (vol. 1, 1919, p. 147): joints oblong to round, 20 to 30 cm long; usually 3 or 4 spines to an areole, sometimes 1 or none on the lower ones and 10 or more on old joints, porrect or a little spreading, never reflexed, the larger much flattened, the longest 5 cm; not told apart as radials and centrals, so stated as radials. Their Arizona plant, O. discata (p. 149), is much the same.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a sprawling shrub 1 to 1.5 m tall and up to 3 m across of flat, obovate to round pads 15 to 30 cm long and 12 to 20 cm wide, new pads rising from the top margins of last year's. Yellow flowers along the top of the newest pads in spring, then purple fruit. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge: about a metre within 10 years. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: green to blue-green pads, areoles 2 to 4 cm apart with one to six white to yellow spines pointing down and tufts of yellow-brown glochids. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): its tepals on a spiral (16 by hand: no flora counts them, and USDA GRIN records 9 to 22 petals on accessions of Opuntia, as quoted in search results; the page itself was not read) on a floral cup above the inferior ovary, from the characters of Cactaceae by the rules at the flowering plants. Its 200 stamens by hand, the most a flower draws, for the numerous ones every flora gives.
